the relationship between grain surface temperature rise and moisture content is monotonic, but is affected by heating time, mass, and container shape.
the temperature rise vs moisture content relationship was monotonic at some sample mass and container sizes.
the temperature of corn, wheat, or soybeans increases in a monotonic manner as the moisture content increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a non-destructive method for determining grain moisture content.
the measurement of grain moisture content by microwave heating.
the use of microwave energy to measure grain moisture content (M.C.).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a monotonic temperature rise-moisture relationship exists for corn, soybeans, and wheat.
the method can be used to measure MC of corn, soybeans, or wheat, provided a sample mass of 50 g is heated in a 100 ml beaker for 30 seconds at a microwave power level of 100 W.
the method is applicable only when a sample is heated in an open container.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microwave heating is a promising technique for indirect measurement of grain MC.
the method can be used to indirectly measure the moisture content of grain if the heating time, container size, and sample mass are kept constant.
the temperature rise vs moisture content relationship is a strong indicator of MC for corn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a microwave oven can be used to measure grain MC, but the method is sensitive to sample mass and container geometry.
the relationship between surface temperature and grain moisture content is not unique to corn and that the relationship is monotonic.
the temperature rise vs MC relationship is not unique for all samples.
